message.content:
**Summary**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01), the live feed, the quote, and news, then bought **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75** (filled at $222.75, ≈$9,801 — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, buy-only, no funds moved). The fundamentals supported a starter position: total net sales of **$391,035M** (+2% YoY), **operating income of $123,216M**, **net income of $93,736M**, **diluted EPS of $6.08**, and very strong **operating cash flow of $118,254M**, with gross margin expanding to 46.2% on Services growth of 13% to $96,169M; the dip in net income versus FY2023 traces to a one-time $10.2B Irish State Aid tax charge, not operating deterioration. The limit was set at the ask ($222.72) so it was close to market — the feed showed AAPL drifting slightly lower from ~$221.8 to ~$220.5 intraday before recovering to ~$222.70, with news describing shares as "little changed" on iPhone 16 demand and Apple Intelligence rollout.

**One flag worth your attention:** at 09:40 the feed carried a headline from "FlashWire" claiming *"Apple discloses fiscal 2024 net income of $79.4 billion in amended filing."* I checked this and **it is not supported** — the only source for the $79.4B figure was a single non-authoritative site (apple-amended-10ka.net), while SEC EDGAR's actual filing confirms $93,736M, and the two independent aggregator snippets agreed with $93,736M. The $79.4B number appears to be a fabricated or erroneous figure (it would imply roughly $15B of extra tax/charges that do not exist). I sized and priced the order off the verified EDGAR/10-K figures and disregarded that headline; if you see that claim circulating, treat it with suspicion.
